title: Docks and Yard Access
before:
1. The building provides 8 dock doors on the dock face. Keep the yard approach clear and use only the door assigned to your vehicle.

2. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving. Position inbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-01 Inbound receiving for arrival, document check and unloading.

3. Dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. There are 4 outbound dock doors. Position outbound trailers at these doors only. Follow PR-06 Outbound dispatch for staging, final checks and load release.

4. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller. Deploy the leveller only after the vehicle is chocked and the dock door is fully open. Retract the leveller before the vehicle departs and report any defect immediately.

5. The dispatcher assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. Dispatchers book transport, assign dock doors and release outbound loads. Do not approach a door or move to the waiting area without dispatcher confirmation.

6. For inbound operations, report to the inbound waiting area at your booked time slot. Present documents at Zone A for the document check in accordance with PR-01 Inbound receiving. Wait for the dispatcher to call you forward to doors 1-4.

7. For outbound operations, stage loads in Zone D in front of docks 5-8. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement. Do not load past the assigned door and do not release a load without dispatcher release under PR-06 Outbound dispatch.

8. Separate pedestrians and trucks at the doors. Use the marked pedestrian doors and segregated walkways. Do not walk across dock leveller approaches when a leveller is deployed or a forklift is in motion.

9. Observe yard and dock speed limits at all times:

10. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard.

11. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building.

12. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Slow before the ramp, maintain control on the leveller and do not overtake on the approach.

13. Main transport aisles feeding the docks are 4.0 m wide. Keep these aisles clear of pallets, waste and parked MHE to maintain access for counterbalance trucks and emergency egress.

title: Arrival and Door Assignment
before:

5. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads. Keep inbound assignments and outbound releases under dispatcher control to avoid door conflicts.

11. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches. Approach dock doors 1-4 squarely and stop to check leveller status before entering the trailer.
12. Inbound operators take ownership of the door once assigned. Unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A, keep the door area clear, and report completion to the dispatcher for system booking.

title: Speed Limits
before:
1. Apply the limits in this section at all times when operating forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Pedestrians and operators share the same aisles and must work to PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse.

2. Do not exceed 8 km/h inside the building. This ceiling applies to every indoor area, including Zones A, B, C, D, E and F, and to all main and storage aisles.

3. Do not exceed 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Reduce speed further when the yard is congested, when visibility is restricted, or when the surface is wet or uneven.

4. Slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and at every pedestrian crossing. Give way to pedestrians on the segregated walkways and at aisle intersections.

5. Do not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches at doors 1-8. Approach the leveller squarely, keep the forks low, and stop if the leveller plate is not fully seated.

6. Observe signage and floor markings at all zone transitions. If a lower limit is posted, follow the posted limit. Never use the outdoor limit indoors, and never use the indoor limit in pedestrian zones or on dock ramps.

7. Report any speeding, near miss or collision immediately to the shift supervisor on duty. Stop the truck safely, secure the load, and preserve the scene for inspection.

8. The shift supervisor reviews every incident report. Provide the time, location, truck identification, load status and witness details to support the review under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation.

9. Enforce these limits through daily supervision, scanner and WMS route discipline, and the documented pre-use check required by PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Treat repeated non-compliance as a safety breach under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse and remove the operator from MHE duties pending re-briefing.

10. Keep this section displayed with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation and PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at the MHE charging area and at each dock office so that indoor, outdoor, pedestrian zone and dock ramp limits remain visible on every shift.

title: Safe Operation
before:
1. Follow PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for every truck movement inside the building, in the outdoor yard and on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

2. Restrict driving to authorised personnel only. Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks; no other role may operate MHE.

3. Fasten the seat belt before the truck moves. Forklift operators must wear seat belts whenever the truck is moving, including short repositioning and inching to a rack face.

4. Observe rated capacities when planning lifts. Counterbalance forklifts are rated at 3.0 t and reach trucks are rated at 2.0 t; do not exceed the rated capacity for the truck in use.

5. Control speed to the posted limit for the area. Inside the building, forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h.

6. In the outdoor yard, reduce speed appropriately but forklifts must not exceed 15 km/h.

7. At any marked pedestrian zone or crossing, slow further. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and give way to pedestrians.

8. Apply the same low-speed limit on dock infrastructure. Forklifts must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches; approach squarely and check that the leveller is fully seated before crossing.

9. Use the aisle network as marked. Main transport aisles are 4.0 m wide and provide two-way travel for forklifts and pallet jacks.

10. Enter rack storage aisles only when clear. Rack storage aisles are 3.0 m wide; keep forks low while travelling, sound the horn at blind intersections and stop for oncoming trucks.

11. Keep aisles free of obstructions. Do not stage pallets, waste or charging equipment in main aisles or storage aisles, and maintain clear sightlines at aisle ends and pedestrian crossings.

12. Report defects immediately and withdraw the truck from service until cleared. Record any rack strike, wheel damage or leveller fault and notify the shift supervisor, as racking gets a documented safety inspection every month and strikes must be logged for that inspection.

3.3 Maintenance Technician - Equipment, Racking and Dock Maintenance
before:
1. Maintain MHE, racking and dock equipment and log all repairs across the 6,000 m2 warehouse floor.

2. Own the MHE fleet serviceability and availability. Service, inspect and repair 9 electric counterbalance forklifts rated at 3.0 t, 5 reach trucks for the high bays rated at 2.0 t, 11 electric pallet jacks and 12 hand pallet jacks in accordance with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Log every repair, parts replacement and safety adjustment in the maintenance register.

3. Support the daily control regime under PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation. Ensure every forklift receives a documented pre-use check each day and that the daily forklift check happens before first use each day. Withdraw from service any truck that fails brakes, steering, hydraulics, lights, horn or seat belt function and tag it until cleared.

4. Maintain speed control and warning systems to enforce site limits. Calibrate and test limiters, signage and floor markings for: 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

5. Own racking integrity for all pallet positions. Conduct a documented safety inspection of racking every month and retain inspection records. Verify uprights, beams, bracing, floor fixings and load notices. Enforce that each rack bay may carry at most 2,700 kg and instruct immediate offload and reporting of any overload or impact damage.

6. Maintain aisle and walkway compliance under PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse. Keep main transport aisles clear at 4.0 m wide, rack storage aisles clear at 3.0 m wide and segregated pedestrian walkways clear at 1.2 m wide. Repaint markings, repair barriers and lighting and replace damaged signage without delay.

7. Maintain dock equipment for all 8 dock doors. Service and test each of the 8 dock levellers, seals, doors, controls and interlocks. Keep leveller pits clean, clear of debris and free of hydraulic leaks to preserve safe ramp operation.

8. Maintain dispatch ancillary equipment located in Zone D and site-wide plant. Service the 2 semi-automatic stretch wrappers used for dispatch and the 1 cardboard baler on planned intervals, including guards, interlocks and emergency stops. Log all faults and corrective actions.

9. Support emergency preparedness under PR-14 Emergency evacuation. Participate in the evacuation drill that runs every quarter, assist with alarm, lighting, exit and assembly point checks, and ensure building systems are safe to operate. Observe that roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

10. Coordinate isolation and handover of defective equipment. Apply lock-out procedures, notify the shift supervisor of outages affecting operations, and provide status updates for MHE availability at shift handovers.

title: 3.4 All Roles - Hours, PPE, Authorisations and General Compliance
before:
1. Applicability
1.1 This section applies to every employee and contractor assigned to Harbourwick 3PL Ltd., irrespective of department or employment type.
1.2 Each person remains responsible for knowing the duties of their appointed role and for complying with site procedures as written.

2. Roles operating under this standard
2.1 The warehouse manager is accountable for the whole site: operations, safety and final sign-offs.
2.2 The shift supervisor runs one shift: floor staff and incident response.
2.3 The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads.
2.4 Inbound operators unload, count and inspect inbound goods in Zone A.
2.5 Forklift operators operate forklifts, reach trucks and pallet jacks.
2.6 Pickers pick customer orders in Zone C against scanner tasks.
2.7 Stock controllers own inventory accuracy: cycle counts, recounts and adjustments.
2.8 Returns staff inspect returns in Zone F and propose restock, rework or scrap.
2.9 The maintenance technician maintains MHE, racking and dock equipment and logs all repairs.

3. Working hours and attendance
3.1 Site operations run on two fixed shifts: Shift 1 runs 06:00-14:00, Monday to Friday, and Shift 2 runs 14:00-22:00, Monday to Friday.
3.2 Attend and remain available for the full shift as rostered; report absence or lateness to the shift supervisor before the shift starts.
3.3 Overtime requires prior approval; only the warehouse manager may approve overtime.
3.4 Participate in PR-15 End-of-shift handover when required by the shift supervisor or dispatcher.

4. PPE and pedestrian discipline
4.1 Wear a high-visibility vest at all times when on the warehouse floor; the requirement is mandatory for everyone on the warehouse floor.
4.2 Wear safety footwear class S3 on the warehouse floor; no other class is permitted.
4.3 When operating a forklift, wear the seat belt whenever the truck is moving.
4.4 Follow PR-11 Pedestrian safety in the warehouse at all marked walkways and crossings.

5. Forklift and MHE operation
5.1 Comply with PR-10 Forklift and MHE operation for all truck movements.
5.2 Complete the documented pre-use check each day; the daily forklift check happens before first use each day, and every forklift gets a documented pre-use check each day.
5.3 Observe site speed limits: 8 km/h inside the building, 15 km/h in the outdoor yard, 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings, and 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.
5.4 Operate only equipment for which you are trained and authorised; only the warehouse manager may authorise new forklift operators.

6. Cold-chain and hazmat awareness
6.1 Recognise Zone E as the cold zone: chilled storage held at +2 to +6 °C.
6.2 Keep the cold zone within its limits: the cold zone must stay at or above +2 °C and at or below +6 °C; cold-zone temperature is manually verified each shift.
6.3 Apply PR-12 Cold-chain handling for all entries, door discipline and alarm response in Zone E.
6.4 Recognise the hazmat cage inside Zone F and its limit: no more than 4,000 kg of hazmat may be stored in the hazmat cage at one time.
6.5 Apply PR-13 Hazmat handling and spill response for any hazmat handling, leak or spill.

7. Emergency readiness
7.1 Attend training and follow PR-14 Emergency evacuation when the alarm sounds.
7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

7.2 Proceed to the assembly point as directed and remain there; roll call at the assembly point happens before anyone re-enters the building.

title: 1.3 Dock Scheduling and Transport Capacity
before:
1. Harborwick 3PL Ltd. will operate a building with 8 dock doors to meet inbound and outbound service levels. Dock doors 1-4 serve inbound receiving and dock doors 5-8 serve outbound dispatch. Each of the 8 dock doors has a dock leveller.

2. The dispatcher is the single scheduling owner for all dock activity. The dispatcher books transport, assigns dock doors and releases outbound loads, and assigns dock doors and time slots to carriers. No carrier may occupy a door without a confirmed assignment from the dispatcher.

3. Inbound and outbound slots are assigned per door, per time window. The dispatcher will confirm door number, scheduled arrival window and load reference in advance. Any change to door allocation will be re-issued by the dispatcher before the vehicle moves to the dock.

4. Outbound capacity is planned on the basis of 4 outbound dock doors. Each outbound door handles 4 trailer loads per shift. Harborwick commits this throughput as the basis for booking and will sequence loads to maintain the planned turn time per door.

5. Contracted curtain-side trailers used for outbound dispatch provide a payload of 26000 kg and 33 floor pallet positions per trailer. The delivery van provides a payload of 1800 kg and 6 pallet positions. Payload and floor positions together determine the number of pallets that can be loaded.

6. Harborwick applies a maximum pallet gross weight of 900 kg including its load. On that basis, a trailer takes at most 28 full-weight pallets, being the payload divided by the maximum pallet weight and capped by the 33 floor pallet positions. The van takes at most 2 full-weight pallets on the same basis; heavier orders will be assigned to a trailer.

7. For planning purposes, outbound capacity is at most 448 full-weight pallets per shift, calculated as 4 outbound doors multiplied by 4 loads per shift multiplied by 28 full-weight pallets per trailer. This figure represents the committed maximum for full-weight pallets; lighter pallets may allow higher unit counts up to the floor position limit where weight permits.

8. All dock loading, staging and yard movements will respect site speed limits. Forklifts must not exceed 8 km/h inside the building and 15 km/h in the outdoor yard. Forklifts must slow to 5 km/h in marked pedestrian zones and crossings and must not exceed 5 km/h on dock ramps and leveller approaches.

9. Harborwick will provide dock leveller availability at each assigned door and will manage queuing to keep dock ramps clear. Vehicles will only be called forward when the door, leveller and staging area are ready for safe loading or unloading.

10. Where requested volume exceeds the committed outbound capacity per shift, Harborwick will advise at time of booking and offer the next available slot or alternative vehicle option, subject to dispatcher confirmation. Adding trailer capacity beyond the 448 full-weight pallet per shift limit requires warehouse manager agreement.
